notes.title: Open Playtest extended until September 18th!
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings, beloved citizens![/h3] 

We looked at all the feedback you left and some of your comments about already yearning to try the game more in the future, and we thought –[i] why not give you some more time to try out the game?[/i]

[b]So we decided to extend the playtest for a couple of weeks![/b] Now you have some more time to join and try out the game, or, if you did it already – spend some more time with a needy giant and not-so-welcoming denizens of the town. 

[img=https://i.imgur.com/y0gLtAZ.gif][/img]

Also, here’s a little tip on some ways to get on the train, in case you haven’t tried those:
[list]
[*][spoiler]There is a back door in the ticket booth, so paying for the ticket isn’t necessary… if you find a way to open it[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Ticket booth cashier fears you, to her – you’re a criminal. Prove her you aren’t evil and she may help you leave the town.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Militsioner won’t just let you leave, this includes even getting the ticket. You don’t have to hide from him though. You can earn his trust, blind him with love, and get on the train before he realises.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Or, if you aren’t ready to commit to courting a giant, your best bet is to run when he sleeps on the job. He doesn’t do it usually though, you’ll have to make some arrangements.[/spoiler]
[/list]

[b]That’s all [i]for now[/i], stay tuned for further updates! Have fun testing![/b]
[i]Tallboys & CRITICAL REFLEX[/i]

notes.content:
[h3]Greetings, beloved citizens![/h3]

[u][b]Gentle reminder, that you still have time to get into the playtest![/b][/u]

You still have two days to explore the town, hide from the Law or… [b][i]Build some meaningful relationships? Seduce the giant policeman?[/i][/b] By any means necessary, catch the last train.

If you haven’t played yet – our playtest is open for everyone, just press the [i]“Request Access”[/i] button on the game’s Steam page. From there, download “Militsioner Playtest” from the library and start your escape.

[img=https://i.imgur.com/QFrHnjV.png][/img]

We also wanted to thank everyone who shared bugreports, feedback and their thoughts about the game! It helps us immensely, especially in fixing all the issues. 

[b][i]So – thank you![/i][/b]

[b]We’re working on new fixes right now[/b] [i](as you might’ve noticed from several patches to the playtest that we released already[/i]), so the experience is getting smoother with each day. 

We’ll share more details about the development in the near future, so stay tuned, there’s a lot of stuff to show.

[b]Take care![/b]

notes.title: Open Playtest Starts Now!
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings, beloved citizens![/h3]

[b][i]Your trial begins NOW![/i][/b] Militsioner Open Playtest has officially started. If you requested access before, check your library for “Militsioner Playtest”. From there you can download it and start your attempts to escape the town.

[b][i]Also, check out our new trailer![/i][/b]
[previewyoutube=7uiUJBtX5QE;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Here’s what waits for you in the playtest:[/b]

[list]
[*] [b]A part of the game’s town[/b] with interactable environment, NPCs and secrets.
[*] [b]Militsioner, the giant policeman.[/b] He ensures you won’t run… [i]unless emotions get in the way.[/i] You are always being watched, but maybe it can help?
[*] [b]Stealth, narrow alleyways, gifts and bribes[/b] – if you want to escape, you should utilize all means at your disposal. Either it's goodwill or sneaky manipulations, brute force or elaborate schemes - the town remembers.
[*] [b]Complete player freedom[/b] – you’re free to do whatever you want, if it helps you reach your goal. 
[/list]
If you played our supporter demos earlier [i](that we post on our [url=https://www.patreon.com/tallboys] Patreon[/url])[/i], there’s will be some new stuff for you as well: 
[list]
[*] [b] New Tutorial:[/b] more immersive and concise, now in the main game, featuring Friend!
[*] [b] New Intro:[/b] with different introductions, influenced by the outcome of the previous attempt and more detailed overall.
[*] [b] Redesigned UI: [/b] updated dialogue system, expanded Mind Map, and Militsioner’s needs are now displayed more clearly.
[*] [b] Townsfolk AI:[/b] now they investigate sounds, panic, but you can negotiate to stop them from calling the police.
[/list]
[i]Stay tuned for our next devlog (that should come out soon after the playtest), where we’ll show new features in more detail![/i]

[b]The playtest will last for 2 weeks[/b], so don’t hesitate to start your attempts today. 

[b]Also we want to remind you that this version of the game is work-in-progress,[/b] many things are subject to change, and you might encounter some bugs. 

You can share your thoughts and wishes in the feedback form in the game, here in Steam community posts or in the official Tallboys Discord server. [b][i]The more feedback we gather from this playtest, the more stuff we can fix, rework or rebalance to make sure that you’ll enjoy our game to the fullest.  [/i][/b]

[i]And while you wait for our kafkaesque game, wanna try some new horror directions?[/i]

[i]You like surrealism?[/i] In Eclipsium you navigate in a trippy realm, where physics and metaphysics unravel and twist in an incomprehensible way. Solve puzzles, get your head around illogical spaces and find what’s beyond the tower.

[i]You like ghosts?[/i] Carimara is a creepy adventure about finding clues and asking the right questions all in an effort to conjure a ghost in this godforsaken village. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3570370/CARIMARA_Beneath_the_forlorn_limbs/

[b]Have fun![/b]

notes.title: Sign Up for Open Playtest!
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings, beloved citizens![/h3]

[b]Your trial starts soon![/b] We’ve decided to open the town’s doors for some time for you to explore – [i][b]We’re collecting applications for Militsioner open playtest! You can already sign up for it on the game’s Steam page and receive access once it starts![/b][/i] There will be a notification for the playtest start, so don’t worry, you won’t miss it. 

Here’s a new trailer in case you missed it:
[previewyoutube="LpxuIwbJLtk;full"][/previewyoutube]

The playtest includes a fraction of the game with most of the mechanics:

[list]
[*] [b]Lonely and needy giant with his wishes, attachments and emotions.[/b] Learn how to keep his mood in check or to hide when things go south.
[*] [b]The town’s district[/b], packed with a variety of NPCs, items and secrets. [i]All is systematic, interactable and changing based on the time of day[/i]
[*] [b]Flood creeping in from below[/b] – when the giant feels bad, the whole town is submerged in water.
[*] [b]Gifts to build relationships[/b] – most items can be gifted, resulting in unique reactions and outcomes.
[*] [b]Stealth to hide from the giant’s wrath[/b] – avoid the light and choose the right time to go for illegal options.
[*] [b]Evading the giant’s hand[/b] – hide under awnings and pipelines and wait for the right moment to run for it. The hand might not get everywhere, but it’s faster than it looks.
[*] [b]Complete player freedom.[/b] Almost every problem has multiple solutions. [i]There are no wrong ways to play the game.[/i]
[/list]

Your task is to escape the town, and you’re free to do whatever it takes to reach this goal. 

[b]Our playtest will last for 2 weeks[/b], so don’t keep HIM waiting, sign up and try to escape the long arms of Militsioner. Or learn the way to his heart…

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1373530/Militsioner/

Please keep in mind – this build is work-in-progress, made for testing, and a lot of things in the game are subject to change: certain areas might lack textures, and you may encounter some bugs.

[b]That is why we’d love it if you share your thoughts with us afterwards![/b] You can leave your feedback in the form in the game, our Steam discussions or Tallboys official server. The more feedback we have now, the better our game will be on release. And, of course, your wishlists are always appreciated.

[i]Hide from him, bargain with him or romance him – do what you need to escape the town.[/i]

[b]Good luck![/b]
[i]Tallboys & CRITICAL REFLEX[/i]

notes.title: Progress report – June 2025
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings, beloved citizens![/h3][p]
[b]Welcome to our soon-to-be regular progress reports![/b] In these we’ll keep you posted on new features and changes that happen in our game, as well as share some development insights. [i]There’s a lot, so let’s get into it![/i][/p][h2]
Crime and Punishment[/h2][p][b]Let’s start with the star of the show – the Militsioner.[/b] First things first, in the latest update we’ve rebalanced his [i]Mood System[/i] and improved his catching tech to be smoother and more physically realistic. Additionally, we’ve expanded his functionality and added more ways to interact with him. [/p][p][b]For example, Militsioner now has an inventory of his own. He stores items in his giant pockets and uses them when he needs to… [i]Unless you steal them.[/i][/b] But don’t expect theft to go unnoticed: if he catches you in the process, this won’t look good in your case file. [i]Not good at all.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://i.imgur.com/d1isDd1.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Now he can also lean in to take a closer look at the town[/b] – to inspect a crime scene or to question witnesses. [i]Or to search for you.[/i] In this case, tread carefully and avoid making noises. Keep in mind that you are a criminal, and if anything causes public unrest… you’re the main suspect. [i]So if you haven’t got an alibi – better lay low for some time.[/i] [/p][p]
[img src="https://i.imgur.com/qqPL0Ty.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]The town’s inhabitants aren’t the welcoming type.[/b] Now if they see you breaking and entering – they won’t hesitate to call the police. [i]To be fair, put yourself in their place: if someone climbed into your flat from the window, you wouldn’t give them a warm welcome, would you?[/i] [/p][p]
[img src="https://i.imgur.com/DpS9Czd.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]If you get away, you’ll still have to clear your name somehow.[/b] When you’re under suspicion, it’s best to  have some friends in town. If your relations with one of the characters are good enough, they can vouch for you and give you an alibi.  [/p][h2]
Loving the Law[/h2][p][b]But, if you’re a law-abiding citizen [i](or slick enough to not get caught)[/i] – you can get on Militsioner’s good side![/b] If the giant is happy with you, he’ll let you wander the town freely. Might even give you some money, if you ask nicely. He can also let you off with a warning, if you were caught red-handed.[/p][p][/p][p][b][i]And, as a new feature, he can give you a lift to the rooftops, saving you some climbing time![/i][/b][/p][p][img src="https://i.imgur.com/y0gLtAZ.gif"][/img][/p][p]Don’t disappoint him though. [b][i]It doesn’t just mean you’ll lose his sympathy. When Militsioner feels down, the town gets flooded.[/i][/b] You really don’t want to be in its lower parts when this happens. [i]Though it can present some new possibilities for you…[/i] [/p][p][/p][p][b]In the recent version we updated the flood system:[/b] now water fills the town gradually, slowly creeping on you from below, obstructing your paths and making some objectives impossible to reach until you figure out how to calm down the policeman. [i]Moreover, if he’s happy, the water lowers even more, opening passages that were inaccessible before.[/i][/p][p]
[img src="https://i.imgur.com/lPLrg3f.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Cycles of Guilt[/h2][p][i]We don’t expect anybody to escape on the first try.[/i] After all, the Law’s hands are long and its eyes are never fully shut. [b]This is why we introduced a progression system, partly resembling a rogue-lite structure.[/b] [/p][p][b]Anything you achieve prior to your unlucky demise will be accounted for[/b] – [i]in your next attempt you’ll be able to change the environment and the giant’s behaviour to make it a bit easier for your successor.[/i] [/p][p][b]With each unsuccessful attempt you earn more currency to buy these upgrades. And with each successful escape you unlock more things you can influence.[/b] Don’t expect the environment to be entirely under your control though. As days pass, certain unique events occur, doors open, bridges get fixed. [i]The town lives on, with or without you.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://i.imgur.com/ka581Kx.png"][/img][/p][p]
[b]To help you keep track of all this, we designed the [i]Mind-Map[/i][/b]: a feature to keep your thoughts, clues and possible routes in one place. Once you encounter an opportunity to progress, [i]be it a ticket cashier who needs a drink or a VHS tape with information about remote parts of the town[/i], it is registered in the [i]Mind-Map[/i], allowing you to return to the task at hand when you’re ready. It also serves as your own database in case you need a refresher on some of the game’s mechanics. [/p][p]
[img src="https://i.imgur.com/5LO33NE.gif"][/img][/p][h2]
Taking a Break[/h2][p][b]For Militsioner it’s not always watching and judging, giants need rest too![/b] That’s why now every four days he gets a day off.  [/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://i.imgur.com/Lp70Yvk.gif"][/img][/p][p]
During a day off, among other things, he’s happier [i](who wouldn’t be?)[/i], and some new ways to get around appear. [i]For example, how about a date with a giant?[/i] You might get to know him better. Good enough to get along and stop this endless cat-and-mouse. [/p][p]
[b][i]…Or exploit this possibility to go about your shady business unnoticed. The decision is entirely up to you.[/i][/b] [/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://i.imgur.com/dKfu8b5.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Town Refurnishing[/h2][p][b]And, of course, there are several changes to the town itself.[/b] [i]First of all, there are two trains now![/i] The passenger train arrives at midday and the cargo train arrives in the evening. They have their differences, but both can be your escape. [/p][p]
[img src="https://i.imgur.com/Lm9aQ2C.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]In some places of the town now you may find a vending machine[/b] with coffee, croissants, mineral water and such. We did this in order to spread items around the map, so you don’t have to go to the same place when you need an item, thus urging you to explore more. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://i.imgur.com/wbYrE3g.png"][/img][/p][p][b]We also reworked cars all over the town.[/b] Previously, every car had its own set of times, now their configurations change with every run. So you can’t simply remember where to get each and every item – [i]after all, immersive sims are all about improvising.[/i] [/p][p]
[b]Lastly, take a look at new game assets![/b] We’re aiming at a down-to-earth, yet somewhat dream-like atmosphere, so the game’s art direction should reinforce it. Every object should look like it has a story [i](that is not necessarily explicitly told in our game).[/i] [/p][p][/p][carousel][img src="https://i.imgur.com/QFrHnjV.png"][/img][img src="https://i.imgur.com/9OjSdhn.png"][/img][img src="https://i.imgur.com/g0Zoklm.png"][/img][img src="https://i.imgur.com/OXwqQ36.png"][/img][img src="https://i.imgur.com/vwc4qPz.png"][/img][img src="https://i.imgur.com/mtp8IdE.png"][/img][img src="https://i.imgur.com/CTOfsoH.png"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p][b]And that is all for this devlog, [i]thanks for reading![/i][/b] We’ll share some more details about the development in the next one, [i]there is always something new.[/i] [/p][p][/p][p][i]For instance, you might want to check out PC Gaming Show presentation on June 8th...[/i][/p][p][/p][p][b]Meanwhile, don’t forget to follow our socials to get the latest news about the game![/b] [i]Or join our [/i][url="https://www.patreon.com/tallboys"]Patreon[/url][i] to try out the game itself – we regularly post new builds for our supporters to try out![/i] [/p][p][/p][h3]Tallboys & CRITICAL REFLEX, signing off![/h3][p][/p][p][url=https://discord.gg/J4KRy5TpNf][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/e5e766adc1dc2acd1408bc51a2af3fabb70acaee.png"][/img][/url][/p][p][url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/CRITICAL_REFLEX/][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/71533114fa83e7ef73a6e15765050fba452a8a16.png"][/img][/url][/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: New Demo & How we made It
notes.content:
For quite some time now, we've been developing a kafkaesque immersive-sim game about escaping the ever-watchful colossal Policeman.
Our last devlog took us through the process of shaping the game's concept, and now, we're all set to finally get to the main course. It all began with a goal: to complete the demo…

[previewyoutube=EPQS7taIFDw;full][/previewyoutube]

Before that, we created prototypes, designed artwork, and established the technical framework, but all the mechanics were scattered. They simply needed to be assembled into one cohesive and enjoyable game. And, Fully determined to reach the finish line, we… kept repeatedly falling into the same pattern—developing scattered ideas and prototypes. It was challenging to break free from that loop, and the situation was only intensified by a part of the team needing to relocate to another country. It felt like we were stuck, this time for good.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/2e9772b1ec5371c18bf15150fbb1a76996a004d1.jpg[/img]

It might sound strange, but we don’t have any intentions of developing this game for another decade.
This means that we just needed to make a new plan - to identify the most basic mechanics of our game and shed everything slowing us down.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/90a5c2deb2e922c7fd4d741d9c47083283e90ba5.png[/img]

So what is the core of Militsioner? It's an immersive-sim about a relationship with the Law. So at that time, actively in development were: an open dialogue system with voice input, a tamagotchi-like mood system for all npc’s, a dynamic time system and a law system.

The main mechanic for elimination was pretty obvious. Keeping up with AI advancements while developing a robust dialogue system became a daunting prospect. By seriously developing an open dialogue system with voice input, we risk becoming outdated even before the game's release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/aa4596419688809ffd8d15cc484448e2f55f3947.png[/img]

We had to abandon the voice recognition system. it was inevitable that some features we had initially aimed for would be cut. It’s natural for every project. While such decisions are typically made behind closed doors in most studios, our commitment to open development means that you get to witness it in real time. But we feel like it's crucial to maintain transparency with you about these unavoidable decisions.

[h2]Immersive-sim[/h2]

There are positives to this as well – it allows us the freedom to really dive deep into the remaining mechanics. So, let’s jump right in!  

All immersive-sims have some form of combat through which its immersion is revealed. Fighting the giant is not an option, so the player will have to resort to tricks - flattering, lying, stealing, giving gifts to appease the giant. His mood is the law, so as you get closer to Giant, different doors start opening up. So basically, we extend the classic immersive-sim staple of "talking your way out of the situation" in to a fully fleshed dating-sim mechanic.  

[previewyoutube=SWnMcMl-Pu4;full][/previewyoutube]

Of course breaking the LAW’s heart is an option too  - you can steal anything not nailed down , including chairs and even bricks from the street. For this, we've created a full-fledged store. 
...Just make sure you're not caught in the act.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/9a4e37df1037295eb0dde9d21e6c31ce8eed758f.png[/img]

To pull that off, you gotta figure out his routine. The LAW needs to sleep too. Time is a key element, everything in the game world operates on its schedule.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/00456debe313af63d5c00ec84c8abd731d70c0c9.png[/img]

It's very important for us that the player experiments and finds their own way to solve each task. But such an approach is very labor-intensive. Typically, in games like Dishonored, each path is crafted separately and represents a complete segment of the game that the player will never see unless they choose that specific route. We can’t afford such expenses. How to maintain freedom without adding years to the game's development?

We decided to tackle the issues in a more systematic way. We introduced universal locks that can be solved in several ways, something similar to what was done in Amnesia: The Bunker. For instance, there's a lock on a door that you can break with a brick, pick with a lockpick, or acquire a key for. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/87a39d770cc80820b32372167eb9fae4b12b16d0.png[/img]

It's up to the player to decide how to get through. Each door may look the same but offers entirely different solutions depending on whether the player has a lockpick, is on good terms with an NPC who can provide a key, or if the player has swiped it from that NPC. Or even wait for the night time and  discreetly break the lock with a brick.

Well, that's it for combining the core mechanics. All that was left was to test it on players, and the demo is ready! ...testing is known to be quick and easy. Games always work exactly as intended.

Numerous logical and gameplay issues arose during regular tests, which had to be promptly fixed and tested again and again and again over several months.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/22381a1c1e368f2c374eacb9910d4fdd10c1592f.jpg[/img]

One of the recurring issues was that people were avoiding the game's mechanics all together. Players struggled to grasp what they needed to do in the game at all, leaning towards tactics they had already seen in other games. They were playing someone else's game.

We fought with this for a while before arriving at the simplest solution: a tutorial!

This small addition drastically transformed gameplay dynamics; people's play styles changed instantly. Mechanics began working, tactics emerged in the game, and players started engaging with tamagotchi systems, building relationships with the city's inhabitants. The demo became much more interesting to play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/b86a6b1f07727d18b983829a1b4162e19e1f5245.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/794ce1a2431bb2e80e280f98e1f47bbbc2995be4.jpg[/img]

After spending several months testing and making fixes, we found ourselves with a demo that felt completely different – more like a real game. We significantly changed the overall loop, tossed in heaps of new content, characters, and details to spice up the game.

The last year ended with participation in the Day of the Devs conference and a ready demo. For those who want to play, the demo is now on our Patreon. 

[previewyoutube=4SxuWCXPDZQ;full][/previewyoutube]

A 10-minute gameplay video is available on our YouTube channel. We aim to keep our development process as transparent as can be, so feel free to share your feedback and join us on [url=https://discord.gg/7gP2hCW]Discord[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38322664/aaa05c19188f7269b3aa974687037c33507633de.jpg[/img]

Hey, this is nowhere near the final cut of the game. The tamagotchi thing still needs some tinkering, the dialogue system is on a quest for a new direction and, honestly, the game's a bit of a walk in the park right now. It's tough to be super objective – our eyes are a bit foggy, but overall, we received very positive feedback. The demo has bloomed into something way bigger than our original plan for these two years, even with the inevitable cuts. Most importantly – we've figured out where to steer this ship next.

I hope the next devlog won’t be named “our progress after another 3 years of development”. Militsioner is soon to be old enough for school; he needs to be set free.

notes.title: Talking with Militsioner #1 - February 2021
notes.content:
Hi, this is TallBoys, the developers of Militsioner game. In this post we’ll talk about the development process of the game and our future plans. We also have a two-minute trailer, showing how the gameplay of Militsioner will feel.

2 minutes of Militsioner:
[previewyoutube=iK47XbFsdqo;full][/previewyoutube]

Right now we’re working on a playable demo. For us, the most ambitious and complex of mechanics is the voice input that was shown in the trailer. We came up with this idea, trying to find interesting and fresh kinds of interaction with the policeman. 

Physical interaction alone is not enough to fully show the profession of "policeman". He can’t keep catching you all the time, so most of your interactions with him must be between the action. It must be some sort of communication with him. Knowing that it would be an important part of gameplay, we tried to find a fresh perspective on interactive communication

[previewyoutube=c4uQktQ-9A8;full][/previewyoutube]

Voice input feels very natural to use, and it can be interesting to play with in the game world: What if you shout at night? If you shout to the car driver? or ask him for help? Maybe try to trick someone? There may be a number of interesting applications here that we have never seen before in any other game.  

[previewyoutube=hT7RRMz-5W4;full][/previewyoutube]

In order for the policeman and the environment to understand the player correctly, we are working on a system that will correctly process the player’s responses based on the context. It is important that it does not make stupid mistakes or create obstacles, as the answers will influence the mood and attitude of the Militsioner towards the player. Similar systems were used in Facade and Phasmophobia.

[previewyoutube=8z8wYir50JM;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]To convince the player of the convenience of this system is the next important problem after the demo. Logically, this is the most understandable input system, but the problem may be in perception: the player is uncomfortable talking to non human objects.

In addition, we’re looking at different voice recognition systems. For example, we’re now integrating the system from Microsoft, which is used in Cortana. Of course, a lot of testing and possibly alternative input will be required, but the priority will be on the system that’ll show itself best in a game.

We also had some interesting news, we collected them here:

[*] We were [url=https://twitter.com/edgeonline/status/1322946681910996994 ]featured in Edge magazine[/url]. We were interviewed by Jen Simpkins (former editor of Edge) about the game’s ideas
[*] Polygon magazine [url=https://www.polygon.com/2020/9/11/21432238/ ]prepared material [/url] (Patricia Hernandez, senior editor at Polygon) about the game , where we also commented  on the development
[*] Russian Federal Channel [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LVUGbedOBnk ]has noticed the game [/url]and they don’t seem to like our game very much. Anyway, it looks funny
[*] This is an interesting [url=https://daily.afisha.ru/brain/17076-kak-razrabotchiki-rossiyskoy-igry-militsioner-prevratili-dyadyu-stepu-v-triller/ ]interview for Afisha magazine[/url]. We talked about the game’s design and little bit about our background. Also we [url=https://dtf.ru/gamedev/211285 ]talked to DTF [/url]about the game’s development (both interviews are in Russian)
[*] Last but not least, [url=https://medium.com/super-jump/militsioner-the-new-video-game-dystopia-upsetting-russian-state-media-bd4fe81a1323 ]а very cool article[/url] prepared by Vlad Alex (Merzmensch), in which he made a detailed analysis of the game and very precisely defined the topics we address
[/list]
